newsitem.title: POLAND: Decision on Espebepe put off to April 14.
newsitem.headline: Decision on Espebepe put off to April 14.

text.p: A decision by creditors on Poland's debt-ridden construction firm Espebepe SA has been postponed until April 14, PAP news agency reported.
The creditors met on Friday to decide on whether to offer the company a debt-relief programme, which would save it from bankruptcy.

"The meeting of Espebepe creditors' representatives, which took place in Szczecin, was not regarded as valid due to procedural reasons," PAP quoted Marzenna Ernest, a judge of the economic court in nort-western city of Szczecin, as saying.

Espebepe earlier said that if creditors refused to write-off 95 percent of its 74.6-million-zloty debt, it would file for bankruptcy. This would be the first ever bankruptcy on the Polish bourse after it was restored in 1991.
The firm's officials were not immediately available for comment.
PAP quoted one of the creditors present at the meeting as saying that Friday's meeting was declared non-valid because not all creditors were notified about it.
Earlier on Friday, Espebepe said that the court rejected a motion for Espebepe's bankruptcy by Stako Sp. zoo, a Krakow-based creditor of Espebepe.
The bourse suspended trade in Espebepe shares on Friday.
